head: 9d4301b05c78d06f16a0d7595022b5a34d9b7f94
classification_reasons: Blast radius is not small: plan.md's Files that change reaches core gate infrastructure that runs at phases (c)/(d)/(e) for every project on the plugin (plugin/gate/checks.py, plugin/gate/diff.py, plugin/state/unpark.py, plugin/pr/description.py), plus the adversarial-reviewer agent, two templates/skills and OPERATING_MODEL docs -- well above 'few files', even though no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is nominally touched.

The code this design prescribes (a rename-aware --name-status -M diff parser, a committed-tree tree_files helper, a new gate check, cross-check union logic in unpark.py) is wholly new; no existing test in the suite exercises any of it today, so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold.

The spec went through a real, substantive correction this round (panel decision #2: the eval-case drop rule could not have been implemented from diff records alone, per the devil's advocate and the reviewer at phase b-1) -- that is the opposite of a tight spec with no open concern; it is now closed, but the history argues for the tighter non-routine gate, not a routine one.
attempted: Intent: re-compared intent.md's Proposed outcome, bullet by bullet, against the current spec.md Requirements and Design (post panel-decision-2 edit) -- phase membership, the test-file and eval-case drop rules (now explicitly 'decided from HEAD's tree, not from the diff's records alone', matching intent.md's own line 39 'nothing is left under its folder at HEAD' more faithfully than the pre-fix draft did), the plan-declared exemption, the risk-list-shaped hit plus accept-risk reuse, the skip-marker listing, the reviewer/REVIEW.md angles, the 'what I need from you' wording and the version bump. All present, nothing substituted.

Spec and plan: read spec.md's Design and plan.md's Files-that-change / Order of work / Risks / Proof specifically for the eval-case survivor logic that the prior adversarial-review round and the phase-b panel (decisions-b.json, panel/b-1-*.md) flagged as unimplementable from --name-status records alone. Confirmed the fix is actually present in the committed artifacts, not only in panel prose: spec.md's Design now names a second helper tree_files(root, ref, prefix) built on 'git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <prefix>' read at ctx.diff.head (committed ref, not working tree); the eval-case drop rule is described as a pure function over records 'and the case's survivor paths'; plan.md's Files-that-change, Order of work step 1/2/3, Risks (second bullet, explicitly citing 'panel decision #2, phase b') and Proof (test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop) all carry the same fix consistently, and Acceptance's eval-case bullet now reads 'empty of survivors at HEAD's committed tree' rather than the prior ambiguous wording the advocate specifically criticized ('passes either way'). Checked the dot-prefixed-rename rule is a separate, still-needed addition (discover() excludes a hidden folder even though the file is not deleted from git's tree) and does not duplicate or contradict the new survivor-based rule.

Proof: confirmed the diff at this HEAD only touches spec.md, plan.md, status.yaml and evidence/ (hook-log.jsonl, decisions-b.*, panel/*, run-b.json, this review's own prior json, diff-b.patch); no plugin/template/docs source file is edited yet, matching phase (b) being the design-only run (the actual code changes are deferred to phase (c)). hook-log.jsonl confirms every Write in this run targets spec.md, plan.md or evidence/panel/* -- no guardrail file, no source file.

Blast radius: confirmed again no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is touched by this commit; confirmed decisions-b.json/decisions-b.md record both panel rounds (the framework/-scope closure and the eval-case survivor fix) consistently with status.yaml's panel_calls: 2, and that the gate's own b-items.json already parked the stale prior adversarial-review-b.json (written for commit d3c983a) as a head mismatch -- this verdict is written fresh for the current HEAD.

Policies: re-checked security-baseline rules 2/6 for the new tree_files helper -- argument-list git invocation ('git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- <prefix>'), no shell=True, same convention as the existing _git/file_at/_cat_ok helpers; data-conventions and most ux-conventions correctly marked not-applicable (no stored field, no UI).

Tests: checked that plan.md's Proof now names a discriminating test for the exact gap the panel found (test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop: one file of a multi-file case dropped while tree_files still lists a sibling at HEAD, expected ok) in addition to the full-drop and dot-rename cases, so an implementation that reverted to the old records-only approach would fail this test; also checked the existing-test-protection language ('no existing test is skipped, weakened or deleted') is unchanged and the skip-marker scan's never-affects-ok guarantee still has its own test and the real --deselect fixture from this repo's runbook tests.
